title: Her first small string band with the Watsons
summary: As a child she played semi-classics in a four- or five-piece string group led by Harry Watson, with his brothers and a bass player named Murray.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: What was the... Can you remember any... Can you remember any straight bands, not jazz bands, that you heard around Paso Christiana? Were there all jazz bands or were there any straight orchestras playing out there?
No, it was a small town. There... Well, we used to play... I used to play with a little group over there, about four or five pieces, and we played just all types of music. Semi-classics and whatnot.
That was your first band? Yeah.
Do you remember who played that then? Did you?
They all did. Eddie Watson, Harry Watson, a fellow playing bass named Murray. And another Watson playing banjoes. Stringes. No horns.
Who got the band together? Can you remember a little bit over there?

That small band? Yeah. Harry Watson was a leader. Oh, I see. He played mandolin. His brother, Eddie, played guitar. And the other brother, Henry, played banjoe. And this old man, Murray, played bass. And I can just a string of them. And we played for various entertainers, which was very nice.
